full_judgment: 3. For proper appreciation of the questions relevant facts may be stated thus: The property described in the schedule to the plaint belonged to Ismail Gazi who married five wives and died leaving a number of heirs through them. Ismail Gazi made a waqf of his property and executed a deed of waqf in respect of the property described in the deed itself. Ismail Gazi put his thumb impressions on the deed of waqf as he could not sign due to his illness and a few days after execution of the deed Ismail Gazi died on 22-4-1939 before the waqf deed could be registered and after his death heirs got the waqfnama registered. Hashem Gazi, one of the sons of Ismail Gazi, got the waqf enrolled and being the eldest son became the first Mutwalli. Subsequently the appellant became the Mutwalli. There were certain property which was left out of the waqfnama but those were also recorded in the R.S. Khatian as waqf property in accordance with the wish of the wakif. For dealing with the excess land a miscellaneous case being Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 1952 was started by the Revenue Officer under section 20 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and out of 81. 81 acres of land in khas possession of the appellant as the Mutwalli and in his personal capacity a total quantity of 36.06 acres including homestead was allotted to him and the remaining 45.75 acres of land was declared excess under section 20 of the Act; and the excess land was acquired by the Government. The mutwalli prayed for release of the excess land upon which Case No. 16 of 1961-62 was started by the authorities, and out of 45.75 acres order was passed for release of 22.46 acres in his favour, and the balance 23.29 acres of land were not released. Hence the suit was filed by the appellant for a declaration as indicated above. The suit was contested by the Province of East Pakistan by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the plaintiff was found in possession of 81.81 acres out of which 76.86 acres were covered by the waqf and 4.95 acres were outside the waqf. The plaintiff according to the existing provisions of law is entitled to retain 33.33 acres of land from the waqf estate and 4.94 acres from his personal estate and the homestead; and the plaintiff has been allotted 36.06 acres in Miscellaneous Case No. 10/52 under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of Camp Jharakhali J.L. No. 45/80 P.S. Amtali, and rest of the excess land, that is 33.29 acres has been acquired by the Government and the same was settled with different persons. Defendants Nos. 2 to 5 claiming to be lawful heirs of Ismail Gazi after getting themselves added as defendants contested the suit. They denied the plaintiff's case about the creation of the waqf by Ismail Gazi and contended inter alia that the waqfnama is vague, fabricated and antedated and fraudulent document which was not excused by Ismail Gazi. Their case is that Ismail Gazi was confined to bed for a long time till his death and be was unconscious for several days before he breathed last. They alleged that Ismail Gazi was literate and there was no need for him to put thumb impression. They claim to be in possession of the property as Ismail Gazi's legal heirs and according to their legal shares.
